ov: Wild dogs of Africa and Eurasia: the black-backed and side-striped jackals of Africa and the golden jackal of south-central Europe and Asia. They aren’t one natural group; the golden jackal is closer to wolves and coyotes.

why.ac: Jackals are crepuscular: most active at dawn and dusk.
why.dg: In one Indian forest district, 220 jackal attacks on people were reported in 1998–2005, none of them fatal.

rg: Central and southern Africa (black-backed and side-striped jackals); south-central Europe and Asia (golden jackal).
df: Opportunistic omnivores: small mammals, birds and reptiles, plus a lot of scavenging.

cf.tip: The golden jackal fills much the same niche in Eurasia as the coyote does in North America; the coyote is generally larger.

fx: Jackals can keep up 16 km/h for long periods.
